Package com.privatechain.core.model

Class Transaction

java.lang.Object
com.privatechain.core.model.Transaction
Direct Known Subclasses:
BlockchainRestController.PaymentTransaction
public abstract class Transaction extends Object
Abstract base class for all blockchain transactions.

Consumers must subclass this class to define their own transaction types. The six fields declared here are present on every transaction regardless of business logic. Subclasses add domain-specific fields (e.g., asset ID, contract parameters) and may carry arbitrary structured data via the protected metadata map without further subclassing (FR-CORE-02).

Why abstract, not interface?

Interfaces cannot hold fields, yet library code must safely access senderAddress, signature, etc. on any Transaction without casting. An abstract class guarantees these fields exist at the cost of requiring single-inheritance — an acceptable trade-off for a value-object hierarchy (see design.md §7.2).

Polymorphic serialization

@JsonTypeInfo writes the concrete class name into every JSON payload under the _type field. This ensures that a Transaction subclass survives a full JSON round-trip on any node that has the subclass on its classpath (FR-SER-01, AC-09).


 // Example subclass:
 public class PaymentTransaction extends Transaction {
     private final String currency;
     // ...
 }

  • Field Details

    • metadata

      protected final Map<String,Object> metadata
      Flexible key-value map for lightweight extension.

      Subclasses that only need to attach a few extra string/number values can use this map rather than creating a new subclass. However, for complex or type-safe extensions, a dedicated subclass is preferred.

      The map is stored as an unmodifiable view once the transaction is built, but the underlying map may be mutated before sign(byte[]) is called.

  • Constructor Details

    • Transaction

      protected Transaction(UUID id, String senderAddress, String receiverAddress, BigDecimal amount, Instant timestamp, Map<String,Object> metadata)
      Constructs a new unsigned transaction with all required fields.

      The signature is initialized to null; call sign(byte[]) after construction to attach a valid signature before submitting to the network.

      Parameters:
      id - unique transaction identifier (non-null)
      senderAddress - hex-encoded sender address (non-null, non-blank)
      receiverAddress - hex-encoded receiver address (non-null, non-blank)
      amount - token amount (≥ 0; non-null)
      timestamp - creation time in UTC (non-null)
      metadata - arbitrary key-value metadata; may be null (treated as empty)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if id, senderAddress, receiverAddress, amount, or timestamp is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if senderAddress or receiverAddress is blank, or if amount is negative

  • Method Details

    • sign

      public void sign(byte[] signatureBytes)
      Attaches the ECDSA signature to this transaction.

      This method is intentionally not final so that subclasses can override it to sign additional domain-specific fields. Callers must invoke the super implementation to set the base signature bytes.

      Security note: The raw signatureBytes array is defensively copied to prevent external mutation after signing.

      Parameters:
      signatureBytes - DER-encoded ECDSA signature produced by the sender's private key over toSignableBytes() (non-null, non-empty)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if signatureBytes is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if signatureBytes is empty

    • toSignableBytes

      public byte[] toSignableBytes()
      Returns the byte array that the sender MUST sign and verifiers MUST verify.

      The default implementation concatenates the canonical string representations of the core fields. Subclasses that add signable fields must override this method and append their own field bytes after calling super.toSignableBytes().

      Returns:
      deterministic byte array over which the signature was (or will be) computed

    • getMetadata

      public Map<String,Object> getMetadata()
      Returns an unmodifiable view of the transaction metadata map.

      SpotBugs flags this as EI_EXPOSE_REP because a Map is a mutable type. In practice the field is always assigned a Collections.unmodifiableMap(java.util.Map<? extends K, ? extends V>) wrapper in the constructor, so the returned reference cannot be used to mutate the stored data. The @SuppressFBWarnings documents this deliberate design.

      Returns:
      non-null, unmodifiable metadata map (maybe empty)
